extracted.intended_audience: news organizations, newsroom leaders, journalists, educators, and the public
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for newsrooms and journalists to demonstrate trustworthiness and transparency to audiences by adopting eight concrete 'Trust Indicators' covering funding, ethics, authorship, sourcing, methods, local knowledge, diversity, and audience feedback. Useful for organizations seeking to build credibility or apply to The Trust Project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Who funds the site? What is its mission? What standards and ethics guide the process of gathering news? What happens if a journalist has ties to the topic covered?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding sources and the organization's mission; publish editorial standards and ethics policies; explain conflict-of-interest handling and recusal rules for journalists with ties to coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist Expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Who made this? Are there details about the journalist, including contact information, areas of knowledge and other stories they’ve worked on?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide bylines with biographical details, contact info, areas of expertise, and links to prior relevant reporting to establish reporter qualifications and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of Work
rubrics_metrics.description: What is this? Do you see story labels with clear definitions to distinguish opinion, analysis, and advertiser (or paid) content from news reports?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label content type (news, analysis, opinion, sponsored/advertiser content) and publish definitions so readers can distinguish editorial vs. paid or interpretive content.

rubrics_metrics.name: References
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the source? Does the site tell you where it got its information? For investigative, controversial, or in-depth stories, are you given access to the original materials behind the facts and assertions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite sources explicitly; link to or provide access to underlying documents, data, interviews, and evidence for in-depth or contentious reporting to allow verification by readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Why was it a priority? For investigations, in-depth or controversial stories, why did they pursue the topic? How did they go about the process?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain editorial decision-making and reporting methods (why the story matters, how reporting was conducted, fact-checking, use of experts, data methods) to increase transparency about journalistic processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally Sourced
rubrics_metrics.description: Do they know the community? Was the reporting done on the scene? Is there evidence of deep knowledge about the local situation or community?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate local presence and knowledge: on-the-scene reporting, local sources, historical/contextual understanding, and evidence that reporting is informed by community-specific expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse Voices
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the newsroom’s efforts and commitments to bring in diverse perspectives across social, ideological and demographic differences? Are some communities or perspectives included only in stereotypical ways, or even completely missing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document newsroom practices and commitments to include diverse perspectives; show efforts to avoid stereotyping and to include underrepresented communities meaningfully in coverage and sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionable Feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: What does the site do to engage your help in setting coverage priorities, asking good questions and finding the answers, holding powerful people and institutions accountable and ensuring accuracy? Can you provide feedback that might provoke, alter or expand a story?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear channels and mechanisms for audience feedback, corrections, tips, and participation in coverage decisions; demonstrate how public input can influence, correct, or expand reporting.
